units: <cite ref="Bava Metzia 26a:10">B. Mets. 26ᵃ</cite> <he>שעשאו פ׳ לשלשה בני אדם</he> (not <cite ref="J00707"><he>ישראל</he></cite>; v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 4) when he made his house a lodging place for three persons (at the same time).

<cite ref="Sotah 10a:22">Sot. 10ᵃ</cite> (expl. <cite ref="A03314"><he>אשל</he></cite>, <cite ref="Genesis 21:33">Gen. XXI, 33</cite>) <he>חד אמר פרדס וחד אמר פ׳</he> one says, it means, Abraham planted an orchard, and one says, he put up an inn (for the reception of travellers); <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 54">Gen. R. s. 54</cite> (with play on <he>א̇ש̇ל̇</he>) <he>פונדיק ש̇א̇ל̇ מה תשאל וכ׳</he> an inn, (where they say,) ask what you may desire, cake, meat, &c.
<cite ref="Makkot 10b:4">Macc. 10ᵇ</cite> <he>הקב״ה מזמינן לפונדיק אחד</he> the Lord causes them to meet at the same inn.

<cite ref="Mishnah Yevamot 16:7">Yeb. XVI, 7</cite> (<cite ref="Yevamot 122a:16">122ᵃ</cite>) <he>והביאוהו בפונדוק</he> (Y. ed. <he>בפונדק</he>) and they brought him (the sick man) to an inn; a. fr.—[Y. B. Mets. V, 10ᶜ bot. <he>אבל בפ׳</he>, read: <he>בפִיסּוּק</he>.]—Pl. <he>פּוּנְדְּקות</he>.
<cite ref="Menachot 32b:10">Men. 32ᵇ</cite> <he>בפוּנְדְּקוֹתֵיהֶן</he> at the door of their lodgings.
